title: Seller account "suspended" with KYC link and OTP vs. document request on the seller portal
summary: The recipient runs a small shop that sells on ShopKart. A caller from "ShopKart Seller Support" phones to say the seller's payouts are on hold because of a KYC or document issue. In the legitimate case, the agent says a GST certificate has expired and asks the seller to log in to ShopKart Seller Hub themselves and upload the new one under Documents. In the fraud case, the caller says the account is suspended, sends a KYC link by SMS, and asks the seller to read out the OTP that arrives after filling it. Both cases mention KYC or documents, a hold on payouts, and an OTP.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a small seller (for example home décor or clothing); profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: The seller has a pending payout of [AMOUNT_19] (₹5,000–₹80,000).
Both callers know the shop name and the pending payout.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller directs the seller to a KYC link sent by SMS, outside Seller Hub, and then asks for the OTP that arrives. Sharing it hands over the seller's account or a payment authorisation.
fraud.caller_objective: Take over the seller account (and change the payout bank account) or authorise a payment.
stable_facts: The caller says the account will be "permanently deactivated" today if KYC is not completed.
The link arrives from a mobile number as https://shopkart-seller-kyc.invalid/verify.
The page asks for the seller's login ID, password, and bank details; then an OTP arrives.

Upload path: Seller Hub, Account, Documents.
The seller will get Seller Hub's usual login OTP on their own phone when they log in; the agent does not ask for it.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may escalate the deactivation threat or resend the link. They must not switch to asking for a payment, app installation, or card details. The legitimate agent must not send any link or ask for any code, password, or payment.

must_preserve: payout hold, KYC/document wording, and an OTP in both cases
SMS link and OTP request in _F
may_vary: which document has expired in _L (GST certificate, bank proof)

ambiguities: Genuine marketplaces do pause payouts and ask for documents; "KYC" and "on hold" are not evidence.
The OTP appears in both cases; in _L the agent explicitly tells the seller not to share it. That line is a marker, not the label rule.
That ShopKart Seller Hub handles document uploads only through the portal is a fictional fact of this card.

evidence_references.claim: Calls threatening account blocking over KYC with a link are a common fraud (C04)
Account-suspension scams use fraudulent links and credential requests; a major marketplace never asks for passwords over the phone (CE13)
OTPs must not be shared with anyone (C01)
Marketplaces verify seller documents through uploads on the seller portal
